newsitem.title: USA: Washington state Senate approves $19.1 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Washington state Senate approves $19.1 bln budget.

text.p: Washington state's Senate on Wednesday narrowly approved a $19.1 billion budget proposal for the 1997-1999 biennium that calls for a reserve of $370 million and $500 million in tax relief.
The budget bill passed in the Republican-controlled Senate on a vote of 25-to-23.
The Senate budget boosts education funding, and includes nearly $500 million in tax relief for property owners and employers, and a 3.0 percent pay raise for teachers, faculty and state employees.
Earlier this week, Washington Gov. Gary Locke, a Democrat, said the Senate budget package was a "good starting point" for budget negotiations.

Locke has proposed a $19.2 billion operating budget for the 1997-1999 biennium. His spending plan calls for a reserve of $304 million and provides $311 million in tax reductions for homeowners and businesses.
The Senate budget now advances to the House for review.
